title: Progressive Output Schemas & Sink Binding — Hosted API PRD (WIP)
content:
Goal
-----
Sketch a developer-friendly model for progressive structured output that can be 'bound' to external sinks (tools, webhooks, function runtimes) while keeping streaming latency low and SDK ergonomics simple. This doc is an exploratory PRD + implementation playbook; not final.

Problem space
-------------
- Users want: low-latency partial responses (streamed) + deterministic structured chunks that can be routed to downstream systems (database upserts, function calls, analytics sinks) without blocking on the model finishing.
- Current limitations: ad-hoc tokens-as-events streaming makes parsing brittle; tool callers expect a single stable contract; SDKs struggle with incremental schema validation and backpressure.

High-level proposal
-------------------
1) Progressive schema envelopes: model emits a sequence of 'envelopes' over the stream. Each envelope is a small JSON blob (text event) that conforms to a superset schema. Envelopes can be of types: partial-schema, final-schema, action-invocation, heartbeat, meta.

2) Sink binding abstraction: developer configures named sinks (e.g., "db-upsert", "task-runner", "logging") on the request. The runtime will: (a) validate envelope -> route to sink adapter, (b) optionally acknowledge delivery to the SDK, (c) apply retry/backoff independently of overall model stream.

3) SDK surface: provide two ergonomic layers: 'stream-line' for simple use (generator-style async iterator yielding typed objects) and 'sink-aware' for advanced use (callbacks/promises per sink invocation + backpressure hooks).

API sketch (request-level)
-------------------------
- POST /v1/generate (body snippet)
{
  "model": "rw-large-1",
  "input": "Extract addresses from text and upsert into customer-db",
  "schema_policy": "progressive",        // enum: progressive | final-only
  "sinks": {
    "customer-db": { "type": "postgres-upsert", "config": { "table": "addresses" }, "ack": "async" },
    "task": { "type": "lambda-call", "config": { "url": "https://..." }, "ack": "sync" }
  },
  "stream": true
}

Envelope example (stream chunks)
- partial-schema envelope (schemaId, fields-known):
{"type":"partial-schema","schemaId":"addr-v0","fields":["street","city"],"confidence":0.85}
- action-invocation envelope:
{"type":"action","sink":"customer-db","op":"upsert","payload":{"id":"usr-123","street":"123 Main"},"sequence":5}

Delivery semantics
------------------
- Delivery modes per sink: sync (block model stream until sink ACK or timeout), async (fire-and-forget with retry), best-effort (no retries, fire). Default: async to preserve latency.
- SDK-visible ACK: SDK can register per-sink callbacks and receive status events (delivered, retrying, failed).

SDK ergonomics (notes)
----------------------
- Goal: make the simple case extremely easy. Typical small customer should do: const it = client.generate(...); for await (const item of it) { if (item.type === 'final') render(item.output) }
- For sink-aware flows, new helper: client.bindSinks({customerDb: handlerFn}) returns a boundStream with additional events: {sinkEvent, sinkStatus, schemaChange}.
- Backpressure: introduce optional .pause()/.resume() on stream iterators and a max-inflight-sink config in client options. Default inflight: 32 ops.
- Type hints: generate TypeScript interface artifacts for the progressive schemaId when model is pinned. Provide runtime lightweight validation (schema-lite) to avoid heavyweight full JSON Schema validation on every envelope.

Operational considerations
--------------------------
- Telemetry: tag traces with sink name, envelope type, model-version, and latency from envelope generation to sink ACK. Measure tail-latency of sink-ack to detect slow adapters.
- Cost accounting: sink deliveries may incur additional usage (invocations, egress). Surface a per-sink meter in usage UI.
- Security: sinks may be customer-managed URLs (webhooks). Provide URL allowlist and optional signing. For private deployments, require explicit trust policy for outbound network.

Backward compatibility & fallbacks
---------------------------------
- If a client doesn't understand progressive envelopes, the runtime will emit a fallback consolidated final payload at end-of-stream (final-only mode).
- Offer a compatibility header: Accept: application/x-rwf-stream+json;version=1 to opt into the new stream encoding.

Rollout plan (phases)
---------------------
- Phase 0 (prototype): SDK iterator + server-side envelope emission; basic sink adapter interface. (2 sprints)
- Phase 1 (alpha): add sink binding config, async/sync ack, TypeScript artifacts generator. Limit to a small customer cohort. (4 sprints)
- Phase 2 (beta): telemetry, retry policies, admin UI for sink configs, docs + examples. (3 sprints)
- Phase 3 (GA): SLA guidance for sync sinks, marketplace of adapters. (2 sprints)

Open questions / trade-offs
-------------------------
- How much validation server-side vs client-side? Server-side validation increases latency. Maybe: lightweight server validation + optional strict mode.
- Schema discovery UX: do we push schema artifacts to client registries or let SDK fetch on-demand? Push favors offline typing, fetch favors smaller requests.
- Retry semantics: centralize retry at runtime or delegate to adapter? Centralized allows observability; adapters may have domain knowledge.

Implementation risks
--------------------
- Extra serialization overhead for many small envelopes might increase egress cost. Mitigation: configurable batching of envelopes to the same sink with max-latency threshold.
- Complexity in SDK causing misuse; mitigate by shipping first-class high-level helpers and strong examples.

Next steps (short term)
----------------------
- Spike: implement minimal server prototype that emits partial-schema + action envelopes for a deterministic extraction model. (owner: Luca)
- SDK PoC: iterator + bindSinks helper in JS/TS (owner: Priya).
- Design: admin UI sketch for sink config and monitoring (owner: Ethan).
- Draft docs / quickstart and three cookbooks: (1) streaming-to-db, (2) streaming-to-serverless, (3) best-effort analytics eventing.

Notes to self / TODOs
---------------------
- Walk through with Solutions Eng this week (Thu 11am PT) — bring design sketches and two example payloads.
- Create Linear tickets for: sink adapter spec, runtime delivery queue, SDK pause/resume, schema artifact generator.
- Check existing hosting telemetry schema to see if sink tags fit current spans.

References and prior art
-----------------------
- Inspiration: incremental RPC/event envelopes (gRPC streaming patterns), Kafka message transforms, serverless function bindings in Azure Functions.
- Related internal docs: hosted-api/streaming-tool-interop-playbook, stream-handshake-snapshot-playbook (note: this doc intentionally focuses on schema-first binding and ergonomics).
